topic.topicDisplayName: Autoantibody panel interpretation: ANA, ENA, dsDNA, ANCA, RF, anti-CCP clinical utility
topic.coverageNote: Open ICAP paper on how HEp-2 IIFA titre and pattern should be interpreted and followed up. It does not cover ANCA, rheumatoid factor, or anti-CCP, so questions stay inside ANA pattern interpretation. A Brazilian HEp-2 consensus in the library was about nomenclature harmonisation and was thinner.

mcqs.question: Beyond a positive or negative result, what extra information does the ICAP paper say the HEp-2 IIFA test provides?

options.A: The antibody level and the fluorescence pattern
options.C: An ANCA ELISA titre as part of the same slide

mcqs.explanation: The paper says the HEp-2 IIFA reveals the level of antibody as well as the pattern, not merely absence or presence of autoantibodies.

sourceRefs.excerpt: the HEp-2 IIFA test reveals much more information than the mere absence or presence of autoantibodies, that is, the level of antibody as well as the HEp-2 IIFA pattern.

mcqs.question: How is clinical relevance of the patterns defined in this ICAP paper?

options.A: Primarily within the context of the suspected disease, and it includes recommendations for follow-up testing
options.B: By a single pattern that diagnoses every rheumatic disease
options.C: Only by the laboratory instrument brand

mcqs.explanation: ICAP says clinical relevance is primarily defined within the suspected disease and includes recommendations for follow-up testing.

sourceRefs.excerpt: This clinical relevance is primarily defined within the context of the suspected disease and includes recommendations for follow-up testing.

mcqs.question: What compartments can show HEp-2 patterns, according to the paper?

options.A: The nucleus and cytoplasm of interphase cells, and patterns associated with mitotic cells
options.B: Only the cell membrane of erythrocytes
options.D: Only neutrophil cytoplasm, as an ANCA test

mcqs.explanation: The paper says patterns include the nucleus and the cytoplasm of interphase cells as well as patterns associated with mitotic cells.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The latter include the nucleus and the cytoplasm of interphase cells as well as patterns associated with mitotic cells.

mcqs.question: How many distinct HEp-2 IIFA patterns does this paper say the ICAP consensus on clinical relevance covers?
mcqs.explanation: The paper presents the ICAP consensus on the clinical relevance of 29 distinct HEp-2 IIFA patterns.

sourceRefs.excerpt: the ICAP consensus is presented on the clinical relevance of the 29 distinct HEp-2 IIFA patterns.

mcqs.question: What does the paper say about antibody level and clinical relevance?

options.A: Level, from titration or fluorescence intensity, has general concordance with clinical relevance
options.B: Level is irrelevant once any fluorescence is seen
options.D: Clinical relevance is determined by anti-CCP, which this paper scores

mcqs.explanation: The paper says that based on titration or fluorescence intensity, the antibody level can be determined and this information has general concordance with the clinical relevance of the result.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Based on titration or appropriate evaluation of the fluorescence intensity, the antibody level can be determined and this information has general concordance with the clinical relevance of the test result.
